source.method: backward walk from today's constituent list through the historical-changes table
notes: `from` == 2016-01-01 means the ticker was already a member at the window start; the true join date is not derivable from this table.
counts.still_member_at_window_end excludes tickers whose chain is broken (end_unknown); the *_including_broken_chains variant includes them and matches a naive point-in-time count of the intervals.

`to` == null means still a member as of the fetch date. A `to` later than 2024-08-31 means the ticker was still a member at the window end but left afterwards; it is reported verbatim rather than clamped.
Only intervals overlapping the window are listed. Disjoint intervals are never merged.

Tickers are matched as plain strings across time. `ticker_raw` preserves the exact Wikipedia cell text (minus footnote markers/whitespace); `ticker_normalized` is the same string upper-cased with any '.' left as-is. No broker-convention dot/dash translation is applied.

not_corrected.problem: WestRock was an index member for most of the window and is absent from the table entirely: Wikipedia's change log has no row for either WRK or its 2024-07-08 successor SW.
not_corrected.why_not_corrected: Adding it would mean inventing interval boundaries from no source. A missing name is never ranked, held or benchmarked, which costs a little breadth; a name filled in from recollection would be traded on dates nobody can check. Missing is the conservative error, so the gap is recorded instead of filled.

not_corrected.problem: Each has no row at all in the change log but a post-2016 Date added in the current-constituents table, so `from` = 2016-01-01 is unverified.
not_corrected.why_not_corrected: All three have no removal row either, which the change log only explains if they were members throughout. The conflicting Date added is most likely a rename rather than a join. Left as reconstructed, flagged here.

ticker D has no add row and no removal row anywhere in the changes table, so the backward walk gives it `from` = 2016-01-01, but the current-constituents table gives its Date added as 2016-11-30. Either the changes table is missing rows for it (and for whatever ticker it replaced), or Wikipedia's Date added reflects a rename rather than an index join. Membership before 2016-11-30 is UNVERIFIED.

ticker ECHO has no add row anywhere in the changes table, so the backward walk gives it `from` = 2016-01-01, but the current-constituents table gives its Date added as 2026-03-23 -- the same date on which SATS appears as an orphan ADD with no removal. These are almost certainly the same membership under an unrecorded ticker rename (SATS -> ECHO). Left UNMERGED: ECHO's `from` is too early and SATS's null `to` is wrong; between 2026-03-23 and now they are double-counted.
